name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Babin running with a large cash advantage
Democrat Rhonda Hart has raised no money
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~93%
model.rationale: Babin is an incumbent in a district that leans Republican by twelve points, and Hart has raised nothing to contest it, so the expected margin sits well beyond the baseline's fundamentals-only estimate. Markets price a Republican win around 93%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Babin would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brian Babin returns as the heavy favorite in this East Texas district, which voted about twelve points more Republican than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with roughly $900,000 on hand after raising over $1 million, while Democrat Rhonda Hart has reported no fundraising and no outside groups are active on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets put Republican chances near 93%. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with the main question being the size of Babin's winning margin rather than the outcome.
